records.name: Paper.principalTheorem
records.entry_name: Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices
records.doc: This project formalizes the main central limit theorem of “Central limit theorem for the complex eigenvalues of Gaussian random matrices” by Advay Goel, Patrick Lopatto, and Xiaoyu Xie (arXiv:2306.10243v2), using an expanded local manuscript as the detailed proof source. The local manuscript was prepared to ease autoformalization by adding details to the proofs. Its main theorem (Theorem 1.3) is identical to the main theorem of the arXiv version: the hypotheses and conclusion are unchanged. Only this main theorem is advertised.

records.name: OverfullCriteria.class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph
records.entry_name: Overfull criteria for edge colouring (Plantholt; Chen–Cao; Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan), unified
records.doc: A thin wrapper that restates, in one vocabulary and with Mathlib definitions only, the overfull criteria proved in PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. class_two_iff_overfull_subgraph: a finite simple graph of even order n with 12 n ≤ 7 (3δ − Δ) is of class two (its line graph is not Δ-colourable) iff it has a Δ-overfull subgraph (odd order at least 3, more than Δ (|V(H)| − 1)/2 edges); this is Plantholt's criterion with Chetwynd–Hilton's 6/7. critical_overfull: a Δ-critical graph (connected, class two, every edge-deleted subgraph Δ-colourable) with 2n + 5δ ≤ 3Δ + 6 (Chen–Cao), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 10 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan, variant), or 3n + 7δ ≤ 4Δ + 17 and n + δ ≥ 27 (Cao–Chen–Jing–Shan) has odd order, is overfull (|E| > Δ ⌊n/2⌋), and so is a Δ-overfull subgraph of itself. The only new proof is the elementary step from overfullness to odd order at least 3 (degree sum) and the conversion to the subgraph form. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: MirekThiele.theorem_1_3
records.entry_name: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.

records.name: MirekThiele.theorem_1_11_hypotheses_satisfiable
records.entry_name: A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators (Mirek–Thiele), formalized in Lean 4
records.doc: A complete Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of the three main theorems of M. Mirek and C. Thiele, "A local T(b) theorem for perfect multilinear Calderón–Zygmund operators", Proc. London Math. Soc. 114 (2017): the perfect multilinear local T(1) theorem (Theorem 1.3), the perfect multilinear local T(b) theorem with general testing functions on admissible collections of paths (Theorem 1.4), and the perfect multilinear global T(b) theorem (Theorem 1.11), for n-linear forms on dyadic test functions in R^d satisfying the dyadic decay, perfect smoothness and qualitative truncation conditions. The development follows the paper's proof of Theorem 1.4 (stopping times, pruning, the telescoping identities, the discrete Carleson embedding and the outer-measure Hölder inequalities of Do–Thiele, the contraction step and its iteration) and the global/local reduction of Theorem 1.11, including the atom estimate for the dyadic Hardy norm for all exponents (Burkholder's L^p bound for the dyadic square function by Marcinkiewicz interpolation). Theorem 1.3, cited as folklore in the paper, is proved by a dyadic paraproduct argument with a dyadic John–Nirenberg inequality for the paraproduct symbols. All constants depend only on the dimension, the linearity, the testing constant and the exponents.

records.name: WaleckiDecomposition.hamiltonian_cycles_odd
records.entry_name: Walecki's decompositions of complete graphs into Hamiltonian cycles and paths
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Walecki's theorem: for every m, the complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian cycles (hamiltonian_cycles_odd), and the complete graph on 2m vertices is the edge-disjoint union of m Hamiltonian paths (hamiltonian_paths_even). Both are stated for an arbitrary finite vertex type of the given cardinality, with Mathlib's Walk.IsHamiltonianCycle and Walk.IsHamiltonian, pairwise disjoint edge lists, and every edge of the complete graph on some cycle (path). The proof is Walecki's zig-zag construction: on ZMod (2m) the paths i, i+1, i−1, i+2, i−2, …, i+m (0 ≤ i < m) are Hamiltonian; an edge {x, y} of the i-th path has x + y ∈ {2i, 2i+1}, which makes the paths edge-disjoint, and m (2m − 1) = C(2m, 2) shows that they cover all edges; closing each path through a new vertex gives the cycles. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Fournier.fournier
records.entry_name: Fournier's theorem: graphs whose maximum-degree vertices induce a forest are of class one
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Fournier's theorem (1973): if the vertices of maximum degree of a finite simple graph G induce a forest, then G has a proper edge colouring with Δ(G) colours (fournier: G.lineGraph.Colorable G.maxDegree under (G.induce {v | G.degree v = G.maxDegree}).IsAcyclic). The proof takes an edge-minimal subgraph H of G that is not Δ(G)-edge-colourable; Vizing's theorem gives Δ(H) = Δ(G), and Vizing's adjacency lemma applied to every edge xy of H gives a neighbour of x of maximum degree other than y, so the maximum-degree vertices of H span a subgraph of minimum degree at least 2 inside the forest, which is impossible (the end of a longest path). Vizing's theorem and the adjacency lemma are imported as lake dependencies from PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009. One statement; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: Couret.Palomar.classification
records.entry_name: Three-point ordered convolution-square classification
records.doc: For three-element finite supports S and T in any abelian group, equality of all labelled coefficients of their ordered additive convolution squares is equivalent to a translation by an element annihilated by doubling, or to the explicit exceptional paired shape in the statement. Diagonal pairs are included. The full proof development is contained in this snapshot. This is an adaptation of an existing public Couret formalization; mathematical novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.name: ErdosUlamProblem.erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos
records.entry_name: The Anning-Erdős theorem: an infinite set of points in the plane with integer distances lies on a line
records.doc: A machine-checked proof that an infinite set of points in the Euclidean plane whose pairwise distances are all integers is contained in a line (Anning and Erdős, 1945). Formal Conjectures states it next to the Erdős-Ulam problem on dense rational-distance sets, which is open; its audience is distance problems in discrete geometry. It is the statement erdos_ulam_problem.variants.anning_erdos of Formal Conjectures (ErdosUlamProblem.lean), which marks it research solved. The result is classical and no priority is claimed. The proof follows Erdős's short argument: for three points A, B, C not on a line, the differences |PA| - |PB| and |PA| - |PC| take finitely many values, and in place of the bound on how often two hyperbolas meet, each pair of values is shown to allow only finitely many points P, as the roots of a quadratic in |PA|.

records.name: KSPalomar.Intrinsic.Full.exists_intrinsic_index_nullity_m2
records.entry_name: KarcherIndex
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the Morse index and nullity of Karcher saddle towers, formalizing results from arXiv:2608.13451v2. For the Enneper-Weierstrass realizations, the two-period quotient Xi_{k,2} has index 4k-3 and bounded Jacobi-field nullity 3 for every k >= 3. For the six-ended family Xi_{3,m}, every positive integer m has index 6m-4 floor(m alpha*)-3 and nullity 7 when m alpha* is an integer, and 3 otherwise. The same threshold alpha* lies in (1/3,1/2), with certified strict bounds 0.4323617 < alpha* < 0.4323619. As in the paper, index and nullity are defined using complex-valued functions, with dimensions taken over the complex numbers. The development constructs realizations from the explicit data and supplies the geometric-to-analytic identifications, rather than assuming the existence of a realization. Supporting results include proper embeddedness and the equivalence of boundedness and finite Dirichlet energy for smooth geometric Jacobi fields on the finite period quotients.

records.name: ArtGallery.agpOrthBoundaryPoint_erComplete
records.entry_name: The orthogonal boundary-point art gallery problem is ∃ℝ-complete, in Lean 4
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of material in a forthcoming manuscript entitled "The Orthogonal Art Gallery Problem is ∃ℝ-complete". A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof, for an explicit single-tape Turing machine model, that deciding whether an orthogonal simple polygon (every edge horizontal or vertical) with rational corners can be guarded by g points of its boundary, which together must see the whole closed polygon (the boundary-point variant), is ∃ℝ-complete under polynomial-time many-one reductions. The orthogonal point-point and point-boundary variants are the subject of the author's earlier entry PALOMAR-2026-11-01-000004 v1, whose definitions this entry reuses unchanged. For general polygons the boundary-point variant is treated by Abrahamsen, Adamaszek and Miltzow (J. ACM 2021); orthogonal polygons are not. The hardness proof is a new construction: the ETR-INV instance is compiled to rows of fourteen relation profiles, and the polygon is a hub with one floor slot per variable and one door per row, behind each of which hangs an orthogonal wing (a staircase corridor ending in an arithmetic room) whose boundary guards copy the slot values through the door and enforce the row relation. Its finite visibility facts are kernel-checked certificates on the wing charts, parametric in the size and value parameters. The proofs use only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

records.name: Couret.PalomarCardinality.fibre_cardinality
records.entry_name: Cardinalities of three-point ordered convolution-square fibres
records.doc: In any finite abelian group G, fix a three-element support S and retain the entire labelled ordered additive convolution square, including diagonal pairs. The number of three-element supports with the same square is h or 2h, where h is the number of elements u satisfying u+u=0; in particular it is at most 2h. The full proof is included. This adapts a prior public Couret formalization; novelty and independent human review are not established.

records.name: TensorPCA.Paper.discontinuousTransition
records.entry_name: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA
records.doc: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.

records.entry_name: Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA
records.doc: We formalize in Lean the principal statistical and constrained-landscape results of Statistical thresholds for Tensor PCA by Jagannath, Lopatto and Miolane, following a local expanded manuscript prepared solely by Patrick Lopatto, the formalization’s maintainer. This elaborated manuscript was prepared to facilitate autoformalization. At nonnegative signal strength in the ordered Gaussian tensor model, we prove the detection threshold below and above criticality for even orders k ≥ 6. For k ≥ 3, we prove the maximum-likelihood value limit at every nonnegative signal strength and the maximum-likelihood absolute-overlap limit away from criticality. We prove optimality bounds for independently randomized measurable unit estimators at nonnegative noncritical strengths, and tensor MMSE formulas at positive noncritical strengths. We also prove the discontinuous overlap transition, consistent testing among fixed nonempty finite families of distinct supercritical strengths, constrained expected and almost-sure energy limits for signed overlaps in [-1,1], and associated variational and landscape conclusions. Almost-sure limits concern fixed parameters and allow arbitrary coupling across dimensions. For interior overlaps, the four-parameter variational reduction establishes equality of infima; unrestricted minimizer attainment is not claimed.

records.name: ConditionalLogRank.stability_probability_pos
records.entry_name: Conditional logarithmic partner ranks in exponential matching markets
records.doc: Switching costs relax pairwise stability by requiring both members of a blocking pair to gain more than a common nonnegative cost. In balanced markets with n firms and n workers and independent rate-one exponential utilities, this package proves a conditional benchmark for ordinal partner ranks in Lean. Fix a matching and condition the market on its stability. If twice the cost divided by log n tends to rho in [0,1), the conditional probability that average one-based firm partner rank is at most n^t tends to (t-rho)/(1-rho) for every rho<t<1; rank 1 is best. Equivalently, the logarithm of average firm rank divided by log n converges in distribution to the uniform law on [rho,1]. Bounded or vanishing costs give rho=0, with persistent dispersion across polynomial rank scales under this conditioning. The theorem removes the original conjecture's supercritical lower bound. The proof also includes positive conditioning probability, exact integral identities, score limits, and rank-transfer estimates. This fixed-matching conditioning does not determine ranks under a uniform stable lottery in an ordinary random market, or dispersion of stable outcomes within a typical realized market. An accompanying working paper presenting these results and their economic interpretation is in preparation. A link will be added here when it is publicly available.

records.name: ReinhardtChallenge.octagon_density
records.entry_name: The Reinhardt conjecture, formalized in Lean 4
records.doc:
This project proves the Reinhardt conjecture in Lean 4. Every centrally symmetric convex disk in the plane has greatest packing density at least that of the smoothed octagon, approximately 0.902414. The smoothed octagon is a regular octagon whose corners are replaced by arcs of hyperbolas. Equality holds precisely for its images under invertible affine maps.

The proof uses Hales's optimal control formulation and builds on the libraries lean4-smoothed-polygon and lean4-optimal-control. It also verifies the construction and packing density of the smoothed octagon.

records.name: IntervalExchange.coe_mkIETEquiv
records.entry_name: IETFree — almost every pair of interval exchange transformations does not generate a free group
records.doc: A Lean 4 formalization of the paper's main theorem: for any permutations π and σ of the d and e intervals, the set of pairs of length vectors (λ, μ) for which the two interval exchange transformations f_{π,λ} and f_{σ,μ} generate a free group of rank 2 has measure zero. The development contains the irreducible case (Theorem 2.6, from unique ergodicity, rigidity by translations and the Diophantine condition), the almost-everywhere Diophantine property (Proposition 2.5, from the easy direction of Khintchine–Groshev), Lemma 3.1 (the length map of the composition is injective and absolutely continuous), the reduction of the general case to the blocks between consecutive pair-splitting singularities (Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3), Lemma 3.4 (a word trivial on a block, obtained by rescaling the block and applying Theorem 2.6 to it), and the assembly of the per-block words into a single nontrivial word. Masur–Veech unique ergodicity and Veech's rigidity are proved as well, by the Rauzy–Veech induction (`IETFree/RauzyVeech/`, `IETFree/Rigidity/`, `IETFree/UniqueErgodicity/`), so the main theorem is unconditional. The remark that follows the main theorem — the relation of a trivial word is robust, so the pairs that do not generate a free group contain an open set of full measure — is proved in `IETFree/Pair/RobustRelation/`: the symbolic data of an arbitrary word and the robustness at a point of the conull set `Ω'` (`evalWord_eventually_eq_one`), and the assembly of the open conull set (`exists_isOpen_subset_hasRelation_of_ae`), which `ChallengeSolved.lean` feeds with the a.e. relation it proves from `main` — the conclusion on `Δ_π × Δ_σ` is `exists_isOpen_ae_exists_nontrivial_evalWordEquiv_eq_one`.

records.name: StationaryMFGChallenge.Theorems.SimplePower.thm_main_simplePowerGrowth_paper
records.entry_name: Existence of stationary mean-field games by monotonicity methods
records.doc: Lean formalization of three existence theorems for discounted stationary first-order mean-field games in positive dimension. Under the paper's monotonicity and respective growth hypotheses, the results give strong solutions for standard power growth and singular congestion, and weak solutions for weak growth. Each result includes density integrability, Sobolev regularity, nonnegativity, identification of the returned weak gradient, and its integrability. The congestion result permits infinite Hamiltonian limits at zero mass and a general continuous limiting flux; the weak-growth result imposes no boundary condition on the original Hamiltonian. The independent Challenge contains the definitions and statements; Solution connects them to the included proof development.

records.name: Erdos881K2.infinite_deletion_of_two_basis
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 881 for k = 2: infinite deletions from asymptotic bases of order two
records.doc: Erdős Problem 881 asks whether every minimal additive basis A of order k (one from which no infinite set can be removed while keeping a basis of order k) contains an infinite set B such that A \ B is a basis of order k + 1. This formalization settles the case k = 2 in the formulation of google-deepmind/formal-conjectures, where a basis of order n is an asymptotic basis: all but finitely many natural numbers are sums of exactly n elements of A. It proves the stronger statement that every asymptotic additive basis of order 2 in the natural numbers, minimal or not, contains an infinite set whose removal leaves an asymptotic additive basis of order 3. The proof splits on whether some positive difference occurs infinitely often in A. If one does, a sparse set of elements in one residue class, each of whose removal is compensated through two fixed shifts, can be deleted together. If none does, elements are deleted one at a time while the representations already used are protected, and a combinatorial argument shows that this process never gets stuck. As a corollary it answers a question of Erdős and Nathanson (1980): a minimal asymptotic basis of order 3 cannot be an asymptotic basis of order 2. The cases k >= 3 of Problem 881 remain open.

records.name: TieredMatching.match_type_concentration
records.entry_name: Concentration of match types in tiered random matching markets
records.doc: We prove concentration of the realized table of matches in balanced tiered random matching markets under men-proposing deferred acceptance. With fixed finite tier counts, positive population shares a_i and b_j, and fixed positive public scores, every participant independently draws a complete ranking by weighted sampling without replacement. The fraction of all couples joining women's tier i to men's tier j converges in probability to a_i b_j. The theorem allows arbitrary tier-label sequences whose counts differ from n times their prescribed shares by at most one. It proves the exact statement of Formal Conjectures PR 7841, corresponding to Remark H.1 in Tiered Random Matching Markets (2021). The development proves the exponential-arrival representation of the exact profile law, the fixed-woman proposal estimate needed from Proposition G.2 with rounding uniformity, and the independent reference coupling used for concentration.

records.name: OAI.TuringRigidity.TwoConeMain.cones_orderIso_iff
records.entry_name: Pairwise rigidity of principal upper cones of Turing degrees
records.doc: This submission strengthens PALOMAR-2026-11-09-000019 and is proposed as the next version of that existing registration, using the same repository and Comparator configuration path. Version 1 states that no proper principal upper cone of the ordinary Turing degrees is order-isomorphic to the whole degree structure. This revision proves that two principal upper cones are order-isomorphic if and only if their base degrees are equal, and that every such isomorphism fixes every underlying degree. Consequently, every individual cone has only the identity automorphism. Both compared statements concern arbitrary order isomorphisms, without regularity, determinacy, persistence, or model-existence hypotheses. The earlier theorem remains valid as a special case; this is a substantive strengthening, not a correction or retraction of version 1, whose record and archived source remain unchanged.

records.name: UnrestrictedBooleanMul.LowHalfMul3.mc_lowMul3
records.entry_name: Unrestricted Boolean multiplicative complexity of the 3x3 low-half multiplier
records.doc: Formalizes the target lowMul3, the three low bits of the product of two 3-bit integers (the product modulo 8), in the unrestricted XOR--AND circuit model of arXiv:2608.30238v1, where XOR and constants are free and either input of a paid AND gate may reuse arbitrary earlier nonlinear wires. Phase 1 proves that the three ANF coordinates agree with integer multiplication modulo 8 on all 64 inputs, and gives an explicit six-gate circuit, one of whose gates reuses two earlier nonlinear wires. Phase 2 adds the derivative lemma (Lemma 8 of the four-gate note in paper/notes/). Phase 3 proves the normal form (Lemma 1), Lemma 2, the pi2 / iota layer with Lemma 8 in the paper's form, Lemma 4 (kernel) and Lemma 6, excludes lambda = 5, and reduces MC(lowMul3) = 6 to four explicit statements. Phase 4 proves the four-linear-gate case (StarFree, Theorem 12 of the note). Phases 5 and 6 prove the three-linear-gate case (lambdaCase_three), so MC(lowMul3) = 6 follows from LambdaCase 1 and LambdaCase 2. The development proves both remaining cases, including TwoClaim and the shared modular feedback lemmas. LowHalfMul3Solution.lean proves the unconditional theorem mc_lowMul3.

records.name: FixedPointChallenge.brouwer
records.entry_name: The fixed-point theorems of Brouwer, Kakutani and Schauder, with an analytic proof of Brouwer's theorem and one through Sperner's lemma
records.doc:
A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem in every finite dimension: a continuous map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space into itself has a fixed point. Also proved: the same for closed balls of a finite-dimensional real inner product space, and the no-retraction theorem, that the unit sphere of such a space is not a retract of its closed unit ball.

The proof is analytic, along the lines of Milnor (1978) and Rogers (1980), and uses no homology, degree theory or simplicial approximation. A C1 retraction r of the closed unit ball onto its sphere is ruled out with the change of variables formula: for small t > 0 the map x + t(r(x) - x) sends the open ball bijectively onto itself with positive Jacobian determinant, so the integral of that determinant over the ball, a polynomial in t, equals the volume of the ball for every t, whereas at t = 1 it vanishes. Brouwer's theorem follows for C1 self-maps of the ball by the ray construction, for continuous ones by smoothing by convolution, and for compact convex sets through the nearest-point retraction. Brouwer's theorem has earlier formal proofs in HOL Light, Isabelle/HOL and Mizar, in Coq for the plane, in Lean 3 through singular homology, and in Lean 4 for the plane and for the standard simplex; this proof is independent of them. A second proof follows Knaster, Kuratowski and Mazurkiewicz (1929): Sperner's lemma for the iterated barycentric subdivisions of the simplex, by counting facets mod 2, then the KKM lemma and Brouwer's theorem for the simplex; Kakutani's and Schauder's proofs use this one, the proof of Brouwer's theorem that both papers cite.

Kakutani's fixed-point theorem (1941) and Schauder's fixed-point theorem (1930) are derived from Brouwer's. Kakutani's: a set-valued map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a finite-dimensional real normed space, with closed graph and nonempty convex values, has a point x in its own value at x; it is proved by Kakutani's argument (piecewise-linear approximations on barycentric subdivisions of a simplex, Brouwer, a limit along a subsequence, then a retraction for general compact convex sets), and a second time through a partition of unity. Schauder's: a continuous self-map of a nonempty compact convex subset of a real normed space of any dimension has a fixed point, and so does a continuous self-map of a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Banach space with relatively compact image; it is proved by Schauder's argument, a simplicial approximation on a fine triangulation of the convex hull of a finite epsilon-net and Brouwer's theorem, then compactness, with Mazur's theorem for the second form, and a second time through Schauder's projection.

records.entry_name: The irrationality exponent of small-height lacunary series
records.doc: Let N >= 2 be an integer, let u_1 < u_2 < ... be positive integers with liminf u_{j+1}/u_j >= 2, and let lambda_j be nonzero rational numbers with log H(lambda_j) = o(u_j), where H(a/b) = max(|a|, b) in lowest terms. The series x = sum_j lambda_j N^{-u_j} converges absolutely, is irrational, and has irrationality exponent limsup u_{j+1}/u_j, finite or infinite. The coefficients may have arbitrary signs, and the boundary case liminf u_{j+1}/u_j = 2 is included, with ratios allowed to approach 2 from below. The proof compares continued-fraction denominator gaps of consecutive truncations. A perturbation lemma places each new gap in at least one of five classes: bounded, inherited, central, short, or reflected. The reflected class gives the estimate needed at the boundary ratio 2. This project formalizes the paper's main theorem in Lean 4 with Mathlib.

records.name: Auto.triangles_in_the_plane
records.entry_name: Triangles in sets of positive upper density in the plane
records.doc: This is a Lean 4 formalization of the theorem that every Lebesgue measurable subset of the plane with positive upper Banach density contains a translated and rotated copy of every sufficiently large dilate of any fixed noncollinear triangle. The proof was developed using GPT 6 Astra Pro. The Lean formalization was generated by Claude Opus 5.5 Medium.

records.name: RegSub.theoremA_l2
records.entry_name: A continuum whose hyperspace of regular subcontinua is homeomorphic to the irrationals
records.doc: For a metric continuum X, a subcontinuum is regular if it equals the closure of its interior, and D(X) denotes the hyperspace of regular subcontinua with the Hausdorff metric. Camargo, Ordoñez and Ramírez asked whether D(X) can be homeomorphic to the rationals or to the irrationals. This project formalizes in Lean 4 with Mathlib the complete proof of the affirmative answer for the irrationals: there is a nondegenerate compact connected set X in the Hilbert space ℓ² such that D(X) is homeomorphic to the Baire space ℕ^ℕ and to the space of irrational numbers. The continuum X is the closure of a countable tree of scaled copies of the Knaster continuum, realized in ℓ² as the inverse limit of the tent map. The formalization proves that the regular subcontinua of X are coded exactly by the nonempty, convex sets of pieces that satisfy a density condition. It shows that this coding is a homeomorphism onto a nonempty, zero-dimensional G_δ subset of a Cantor cube in which every compact set has empty interior. It then concludes with the Alexandrov–Urysohn characterization of the Baire space and the homeomorphism between ℕ^ℕ and the irrationals. Both classical results are also proved in the project.

records.name: IdealGenerationPaper.main_result
records.entry_name: Ideal generation for general reduced projective points
records.doc: Formalizes Theorem 1.1 of Ideal Generation for General Reduced Projective Points. Over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, for every projective dimension n >= 1, degree D >= 2 and point count between binomial(n+D-1,D-1) and binomial(n+D,D)-1, a nonempty principal open of ordered reduced point configurations has maximal-rank multiplication from I_D tensor S_1 to I_(D+1). The homogeneous ideal has the exact predicted numbers of minimal generators in degrees D and D+1 and is generated in those degrees. Generality is expressed in the standard affine chart of projective space. The points are actual projective classes and their homogeneous ideal is radical.

records.name: OeisA60841.conjecture1
records.entry_name: OEIS A060841: 1/det(1/lcm(i,j)) is an integer exactly for n <= 34, n = 36 and n = 38
records.doc: Let M be the n x n matrix with entries 1/lcm(i,j). R. G. Wilson v conjectured (OEIS A060841, 2015) that 1/det(M) is an integer only for n = 1, ..., 34, 36 and 38. This project proves the conjecture as stated in formal-conjectures (OeisA60841.conjecture1): by Smith's determinant the gcd matrix factors as E diag(phi) E^T with E the unitriangular divisibility matrix, so 1/det(M) = (n!)^2 / prod_{k <= n} phi(k); for n in {1, ..., 34, 36, 38} the divisibility is decided by computation, and for every other n the odd primes up to 97 and the powers of 2 from 4 to 128 force v_2(prod phi(k)) > v_2((n!)^2), numerically for n = 35, 37 and 39 <= n < 100 and by a linear bound for n >= 100.

records.name: PalomarIngham.zeta_ne_zero_iff_psi_error
records.entry_name: Ingham's theorem: zero-free half-planes of the Riemann zeta function and the error term in the prime number theorem
records.doc: For 1/2 ≤ θ < 1, the Riemann zeta function has no zeros with real part greater than θ if and only if Chebyshev's ψ(x) = x + O(x^{θ+δ}) for every δ > 0. Consequences: the Riemann hypothesis is equivalent to ψ(x) = x + O(x^{1/2+δ}) for all δ > 0, and the zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 (proved by OpenAI in 2026, used here as an explicitly stated hypothesis) yields ψ(x) = x + O(x^{7/8+δ}). Both directions are proved: the easy direction by partial summation and holomorphy of a Mellin transform; the hard direction by a smoothed Chebyshev function, a contour shift to a vertical line inside the zero-free half-plane, and a bound ζ'/ζ(σ+it) ≪ log|t| obtained from the Borel–Carathéodory theorem.

records.name: PalomarLRX.boundedRouting
records.entry_name: Exact LRX diameter of the symmetric group
records.doc: For every n >= 4 the Cayley graph of S_n with unit-cost generators L = (0 1 ... n-1), R = L inverse, and X = (0 1) has diameter n*(n-1)/2. The formalization proves upper and lower bounds and a literal L/R/X word of at most that length between every ordered pair of permutations. The independent Challenge defines the moves, their word evaluation, and the undirected Cayley graph using Mathlib alone.

records.name: OeisA100475.conjecture
records.entry_name: OEIS A100475: the reverse-prime map never loops
records.doc: Let f(y) be the decimal reversal of the y-th prime (f(1) = 2, f(2) = 3, f(5) = 11, f(11) = 13). OEIS A100475 is the orbit of 1 under f, and its entry asks (Jonathan Vos Post, 2004) whether the orbit of any other positive start ever enters a loop. This project proves that it never does, i.e. the negation of the formal-conjectures statement OeisA100475.conjecture: the number of digits never decreases along an orbit (p_y > y, and a prime never ends in 0), so on a cycle it is a constant D and every cycle element v satisfies p_v < 10^D; for D <= 4 this forces v <= 1229, and a kernel-checked table of the first 1230 primes with an escape-time ranking shows that no cycle stays below 1230; for D >= 5 it contradicts the bound pi'(10^D) < 10^(D-1) on the number of primes below 10^D, proved for D = 5, ..., 8 by Legendre's sieve recursion evaluated by the Lean kernel and for D >= 9 by Chebyshev's bound theta(x) <= x log 4 with the split point 10^(D-2).

records.name: Erdos670.erdos_670.variants.tripodo
records.entry_name: Separated distances in the fixed space R^29
records.doc: For every natural N there is n at least N and an n-point set in the single fixed Euclidean space R^29 whose distances on different unordered pairs of distinct points differ by at least one, with diameter strictly below (499/500)n^2. The sizes n form an unbounded set; no claim is made for every large n. As a consequence the formalization proves the negation of the fixed-dimension proposition for Erdős Problem 670 exactly as stated in Formal Conjectures at commit 2f91d251c07fbbaf9435166d47c11e884a08a6cf, using d = 29 and epsilon = 1/1000. No optimality, smallest dimension or independent priority review is claimed.

records.name: Erdos1017.uniform_asymptotic
records.entry_name: Erdős Problem 1017: clique partitions of graphs of given size
records.doc: A Lean proof that f(n, k), the least number such that the edges of every graph with n vertices and k edges can be partitioned into at most f(n, k) cliques, satisfies f(n, k) = n² B(k/n²) + o(n²) uniformly in 0 ≤ k ≤ n(n − 1)/2, for an explicit continuous piecewise-algebraic function B on [0, 1/2]. B(d) = d for d ≤ 1/4; above 1/4 it is the larger of two curves built from explicit dual certificates on split, mixed and two-head graphs. This provides an asymptotic resolution of Erdős Problem 1017, as posed by Erdős and as stated by Bloom, who asks for an estimate of f(n, k) for k > n²/4. The formula is new to our knowledge. The proof passes through the fractional relaxation and proves again, in Lean, the case of the fractional-to-integral transfer of Balogh, He, Krueger, Nguyen and Wigal that it needs.

records.name: ArtinMatthewsPaper.main_result
records.entry_name: An Unconditional Artin–Matthews Theorem for Simultaneous Primitive Roots
records.doc: For a nonempty finite set of integers excluding 0, 1, and −1, consider the primes for which every integer in the set is a primitive root. When neither Matthews obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes have a lower bound of order x/log x in every sufficiently large real dyadic interval (x, 2x] and positive lower relative density among the primes. When either obstruction occurs, the simultaneous primitive primes form a finite set. This is Theorem 1.1 of the accompanying paper.

records.name: RamanujanCongruences.congr_of
records.entry_name: Ramanujan's congruences for the one-dimensional cusp spaces
records.doc: A general theorem and its six instances. The theorem (congr_of): let k = 12 + 4a + 6b; if the space M_{k−12} of level-one modular forms has rank one and 2k/B_k = D/ℓ with ℓ and D coprime integers, then the q-expansion coefficients of Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b are integers congruent to σ_{k−1}(n) modulo ℓ, for every n. The hypothesis holds exactly for k = 12, 16, 18, 20, 22, 26, where the cusp space is spanned by this one form, and the instances are the congruences modulo the numerator of B_k/2k: 691, 3617, 43867, 174611 = 283·617, 77683 = 131·593 and 657931. The case k = 12 is Ramanujan's τ(n) ≡ σ₁₁(n) (mod 691); the other five are the remaining congruences of this kind at level one. The statements are for every n and use only Mathlib definitions; the Bernoulli numbers B_12 to B_26 are computed in Lean, not assumed. Integrality comes from the product formula for Δ, expanded by Mathlib's pentagonal number theorem, and the integer coefficients 240σ₃ and −504σ₅ of E₄ and E₆. The congruence comes from one exact identity in M_k: E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k vanishes at the cusp, so dividing by Δ (Mathlib's discriminantEquiv) gives a form in M_{k−12}, which is one-dimensional and spanned by E₄^a·E₆^b; hence E₄^(a+3)·E₆^b − E_k = c·Δ·E₄^a·E₆^b, with c read off from the q¹-coefficient. Since E_k = 1 − (2k/B_k)∑σ_{k−1}(n)qⁿ, multiplying by the numerator of B_k/2k and reducing shows that the Eisenstein series is congruent to the cusp form. The argument is proved once for general (a, b) and applied to the six cases.

records.name: ZP.zp_quasihalts_iff_sentence
records.entry_name: A beeping busy beaver machine for the Σ₂ form of P vs NP
records.doc: Explicit one-tape, two-symbol Turing machines with a designated beep state (Aaronson's beeping busy beaver convention), given as literal transition tables, together with core-Lean proofs (no Mathlib) that each machine, run from the blank tape, beeps only finitely often exactly when a stated Sigma_2 sentence holds. The flagship machine (278 states) is equivalent to the Sigma_2 form of P = NP: some candidate program decides a fixed self-padded NP-complete language within a polynomial clock on every instance. The equivalence of that sentence with P = NP is also proved in Lean (ZP.Cx.sentence_iff_PeqNP) for the Turing-machine models defined in the development. The same guest interpreter yields machines for further Sigma_2 statements: P = PP and P = PSPACE, factoring, discrete logarithm, graph isomorphism, an NTT-based variant over least primes 1 + n i, linear-time integer multiplication on multitape machines, a co-NP verifier variant, promise-P = promise-BPP, NP in P/poly, deterministic and nondeterministic multihead log-space (L = NL), and linear-time multiplication of matrices over GF(2) on multitape machines. A 19-state machine quasihalts iff there are finitely many twin primes.

records.doc: Explicit one-tape, two-symbol Turing machines with a designated beep state (Aaronson's beeping busy beaver convention), given as literal transition tables, together with core-Lean proofs (no Mathlib) that each machine, run from the blank tape, beeps only finitely often exactly when a stated Sigma_2 sentence holds. The flagship machine (278 states) is equivalent to the Sigma_2 form of P = NP: some candidate program decides a fixed self-padded NP-complete language within a polynomial clock on every instance. The equivalence of that sentence with P = NP is also proved in Lean (ZP.Cx.sentence_iff_PeqNP) for the Turing-machine models defined in the development. The same guest interpreter yields machines for further Sigma_2 statements: P = PP and P = PSPACE, factoring, discrete logarithm, graph isomorphism, an NTT-based variant over least primes 1 + n i, linear-time integer multiplication on multitape machines, a co-NP verifier variant, promise-P = promise-BPP, NP in P/poly, deterministic and nondeterministic multihead log-space (L = NL), and linear-time multiplication of matrices over GF(2) on multitape machines. A 19-state machine quasihalts iff there are finitely many twin primes.

records.name: RegularSubcontinua.isRegSubcontinuum_iff_exists_mem_regular
records.entry_name: On the structure of countable hyperspaces of regular subcontinua
records.doc: For a metric continuum X, D(X) is the hyperspace of subcontinua of X that are the closure of their interior, with the Hausdorff metric. The project formalizes the theorem that a countable D(X) is a G-delta subset of the hyperspace of subcontinua, hence completely metrizable and scattered with dense isolated points, so that D(X) is never homeomorphic to the rationals; together with the structure theory behind it (independent families, blister theorem, complement lemma, absorption by minimal elements, decreasing intersections, density of minimal elements, D-atomic continua, the cardinality dichotomy).

records.name: JordanPrime.jordan_onto_prime
records.entry_name: Herstein's theorem on Jordan homomorphisms onto prime rings, in Smiley's form for characteristic different from 2 and in his form for every characteristic, with the Jacobson-Rickart domain theorem and an example for each hypothesis
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of six statements. An additive map phi between associative rings is a Jordan homomorphism when phi(ab + ba) = phi(a)phi(b) + phi(b)phi(a). (1) A Jordan homomorphism onto a prime ring without 2-torsion is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism (phi(ab) = phi(b)phi(a)): Herstein's theorem (1956, Theorem H) in the form Smiley gave it (1957, p. 428), with characteristic 3 admitted; an additive map of rings, no identity assumed. (2) The domain form in every characteristic (Jacobson and Rickart 1950, Theorem 2): an additive map with phi(a^2) = phi(a)^2 and phi(aba) = phi(a)phi(b)phi(a), into a ring without zero divisors, is multiplicative or anti-multiplicative, with no surjectivity and no hypothesis on 2. (3)-(5) Each hypothesis of (1) is needed; each statement asserts that one hypothesis fails, that the others hold, and that the map is neither multiplicative nor anti-multiplicative: (3) from 2x2 into 4x4 integer matrices, not onto, the target prime and without 2-torsion (witness a -> diag(a, a^T)); (4) on pairs of 2x2 integer matrices, onto, the target not prime (witness (a, b) -> (a, b^T)); (5) from F_2 x F_2 onto F_2, a prime ring with 2-torsion (witness (x, y) -> x + y). (6) The theorem in every characteristic (Smiley 1957, Added in proof, p. 429): an additive map with the two identities of (2), onto a prime ring, is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with no hypothesis on 2; it implies (1), and (5) shows that the Jordan identity alone does not suffice when the ring has 2-torsion. The compared statements add no definition: the identities on the map and the conditions on the target ring are written out as universally quantified statements, the maps are Mathlib's AddMonoidHom, and onto is Function.Surjective. Statements 1, 2 and 6 formalize theorems of the 1950s and statements 3-5 are standard examples; nothing here is a new theorem. The proof of (1) follows the argument written out by Beidar, Bresar and Chebotar (2003, Proposition 3.1), not Smiley's; the proof of (2) is Jacobson and Rickart's; the proof of (6) is Smiley's, through his lemma that a prime ring in which every commutator squares to zero is commutative. Not formalized: the semiprime generalizations. A prior formalization of the case of complex-linear maps between unital complex algebras exists in github.com/openai/math and is recorded under related_formalizations; statements (1) and (6) contain that case. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): the self-adjoint elements of an algebra of observables are closed under the symmetrized product and not, in general, under the product; applied to the identity map, (1) says that on a prime ring without 2-torsion the symmetrized product determines the associative product up to reversing the order of the factors.

(2) The domain form in every characteristic (Jacobson and Rickart 1950, Theorem 2): an additive map with phi(a^2) = phi(a)^2 and phi(aba) = phi(a)phi(b)phi(a), into a ring without zero divisors, is multiplicative or anti-multiplicative, with no surjectivity and no hypothesis on 2. (3)-(5) Each hypothesis of (1) is needed; each statement asserts that one hypothesis fails, that the others hold, and that the map is neither multiplicative nor anti-multiplicative: (3) from 2x2 into 4x4 integer matrices, not onto, the target prime and without 2-torsion (witness a -> diag(a, a^T)); (4) on pairs of 2x2 integer matrices, onto, the target not prime (witness (a, b) -> (a, b^T)); (5) from F_2 x F_2 onto F_2, a prime ring with 2-torsion (witness (x, y) -> x + y). (6) The theorem in every characteristic (Smiley 1957, Added in proof, p. 429): an additive map with the two identities of (2), onto a prime ring, is a homomorphism or an anti-homomorphism, with no hypothesis on 2; it implies (1), and (5) shows that the Jordan identity alone does not suffice when the ring has 2-torsion. The compared statements add no definition: the identities on the map and the conditions on the target ring are written out as universally quantified statements, the maps are Mathlib's AddMonoidHom, and onto is Function.Surjective. Statements 1, 2 and 6 formalize theorems of the 1950s and statements 3-5 are standard examples; nothing here is a new theorem. The proof of (1) follows the argument written out by Beidar, Bresar and Chebotar (2003, Proposition 3.1), not Smiley's; the proof of (2) is Jacobson and Rickart's; the proof of (6) is Smiley's, through his lemma that a prime ring in which every commutator squares to zero is commutative. Not formalized: the semiprime generalizations. A prior formalization of the case of complex-linear maps between unital complex algebras exists in github.com/openai/math and is recorded under related_formalizations; statements (1) and (6) contain that case. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): the self-adjoint elements of an algebra of observables are closed under the symmetrized product and not, in general, under the product; applied to the identity map, (1) says that on a prime ring without 2-torsion the symmetrized product determines the associative product up to reversing the order of the factors.

records.name: AllCollapse.all_bernoulli_shifts_isomorphic
records.entry_name: A countable group all of whose nontrivial Bernoulli shifts are isomorphic
records.doc: There is a countable group G such that the Bernoulli shifts of G with bases (L, lambda) and (L', lambda') are isomorphic for all standard probability spaces whose measures are not point masses: there is an equivariant, measure-preserving bijection, measurable in both directions, between shift-invariant measurable sets of full measure. No condition is put on the entropies of the bases, which may differ and may be infinite. The group is N x (Z/2 wr Z), where N is the group of the pinned OpenAI construction, which supplies the algebraic existence input. This formalization does not certify finitary or continuous conjugacy and says nothing about other groups.

records.name: FlatConformalKilling.conformalKilling_iff_family
records.entry_name: Conformal Killing and Killing fields of flat pseudo-Euclidean space: classification for n >= 3 in every signature, the two dimension counts, and the divergence of the current of a symmetric tensor field
records.doc: Kernel-checked proofs, in Lean 4 + Mathlib, of nine statements about R^n with a diagonal metric eta whose entries are +1 or -1 (every signature). A covector field omega is conformal Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 2 phi eta_ij for some function phi, and Killing when it is C^3 and d_i omega_j + d_j omega_i = 0. (1) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields are exactly the members of an explicit family: translations, rotations (an antisymmetric matrix), the dilation and the special conformal fields. (2) In every dimension the Killing fields are exactly the affine fields a + A x with A antisymmetric. (3) For n >= 3 the conformal Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension (n+1)(n+2)/2. (4) In every dimension the Killing fields form a real vector space of finite dimension n(n+1)/2. (5) A control for the hypothesis n >= 3 of (1): in the Euclidean plane there is a conformal Killing field that is not a member of the family for any values of its parameters, the matrix being any real matrix, antisymmetric or not (the witness in the proof is the real and imaginary parts of z^3). Statements (6)-(9) are statements about conserved currents: they say which fields give conserved currents. (6) If a tensor field T and a covector field omega are differentiable at a point x, T(x) is symmetric and the conformal Killing equation holds at x with factor phi, then the current J^i = sum_j T^ij omega_j satisfies div J = (div T) . omega + phi tr_eta T at x. (7) A C^3 field is conformal Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free, eta-trace-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (8) A C^3 field is Killing if and only if the current of every differentiable, symmetric, divergence-free tensor field against it is divergence-free. (9) For n >= 1 the dilation omega_j = eta_j x_j is conformal Killing and is not Killing. The Challenge imports Mathlib only and carries the definitions its statements use (the partial derivative, the two equations, the family, the two solution spaces as submodules, the divergences, the current and the metric trace), each with its convention. Statements (1)-(4) are classical: (1) and (3) are the classification of the conformal Killing fields of R^{p,q}, p + q >= 3, and the count of their parameters (Schottenloher 2008, Theorem 1.7; Ginsparg 1988, section 1.1), the infinitesimal counterpart of Liouville's theorem on conformal maps; (2) and (4) are the Killing fields of flat space and their number. (6) is the standard identity behind the conserved currents of a trace-free stress tensor, and (5) and (9) are standard examples. In (7) and (8) the direction from the equation to conserved currents is (6); the other direction was not found stated in the sources read for this entry, is elementary (it is proved by testing on constant tensor fields, so it is a pointwise fact of linear algebra) and is not claimed as new. No statement is claimed as a new theorem. Scope: diagonal metrics with entries +1 or -1 (a general constant metric, reached by a linear change of coordinates, is not formalized); C^3 covector fields on all of R^n; the numbers in (3) and (4) are dimensions of real vector spaces, with no Lie bracket and no isomorphism with so(p+1,q+1) stated; the finite conformal maps (Liouville's theorem itself) are not formalized; nothing is said about compactly supported tensor fields in (7) and (8). Prior formalization, recorded under related_formalizations: the identity (6), with its corollary for conserved trace-free tensors, is formalized for n = 4 and signature (1,3), for tensors of tempered distributions, in github.com/openai/math; special cases of the currents are in the Yang-Mills release github.com/yang-mills-group/OpenAI-YM-20261028 and in facebookresearch/atlas-lean, and Killing fields on Riemannian manifolds are in atlas-lean and in TauCetiProject/TauCeti. In a dated search no formalization was found of (1)-(5) or of the direction of (7) and (8) from conserved currents to the equation. Application (cited; no compared statement asserts it): for n = 4 and a Lorentzian signature the spaces of (3) and (4) have dimensions 15 and 10, the infinitesimal conformal symmetries and the infinitesimal isometries of Minkowski space, and (6) is the conservation law for the currents of a conserved symmetric stress tensor against them, trace-free in the conformal case.

records.name: GwResidue.theorem1
records.entry_name: Gallai–van der Waerden numbers from quadratic-residue colourings
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of a lower-bound construction for the Gallai–van der Waerden numbers GW(r; 3, l) of Mao, Ozeki, Robertson and Wang: the least m such that for every n ≥ m, every exact r-colouring of {1, …, n} contains a rainbow 3-term or a monochromatic l-term arithmetic progression. Theorem 1: let l ≥ 4 and let p > l be a prime with p ≡ 1 (mod 8) such that no l consecutive integers in [1, p − 1] have the same Legendre symbol modulo p; let s ≥ 2 and let z colour {0, …, l − 1} onto s colours with no rainbow 3-term progression. Colour x in [1, (l − 1)p + 1] by its quadratic character of x − 1 (two colours) when x ≢ 1 (mod p), and the point x = 1 + kp by the new colour 2 + z(k). This colouring uses all s + 2 colours and has no rainbow 3-term and no monochromatic l-term progression, so GW(s + 2; 3, l) > (l − 1)p + 1. The formalization proves Theorem 1 for every such l, p, s and z, the resulting bound for GW (unconditionally for every threshold with the defining property, and for the number itself given that a threshold exists), and the instance (l, p) = (4, 17), which gives GW(4; 3, 4) > 52 and GW(5; 3, 4) > 52.

records.name: LovaszGF.lovasz_gf_factor
records.entry_name: Lovász's (g,f)-factor theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Lovász's (g,f)-factor theorem (1970): for a finite simple graph G and g ≤ f : V → ℕ, G has a spanning subgraph H with g(v) ≤ deg_H(v) ≤ f(v) for every vertex if and only if, for all disjoint vertex sets S and T, h(S,T) ≤ Σ_{v∈S} f(v) + Σ_{v∈T} (deg_{G−S}(v) − g(v)), where h(S,T) is the number of components C of G − (S ∪ T) with g = f on C and Σ_{v∈C} f(v) + e(C,T) odd (lovasz_gf_factor). As a corollary, the criterion of Heinrich, Hell, Kirkpatrick and Liu for g < f, without the component term (gf_factor_of_lt). The proof reduces the theorem to Tutte's f-factor theorem, imported as a lake dependency from PALOMAR-2026-10-18-000005, through a gadget: f(v) − g(v) slack vertices are joined to each vertex v, and the slack vertices together with one extra vertex form a clique, with target degree 1 on slack vertices and (Σ g) mod 2 on the extra vertex. One definition beyond Mathlib's (h(S,T), tightOddCount); g and f are natural-number valued.

records.name: SiegelThm.siegel
records.entry_name: Siegel's theorem on L(1, χ) for real Dirichlet characters
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Siegel's theorem (1935): for every ε > 0 there is c > 0 with c·N^(-ε) ≤ ‖L(1, χ)‖ for every real non-principal Dirichlet character χ modulo N (SiegelThm.siegel, with Mathlib's DirichletCharacter.LFunction; χ need not be primitive). The proof is Goldfeld's (1974): F = ζ·L(χ₁)L(χ₂)L(χ₁χ₂) has non-negative Dirichlet coefficients with a₁ = 1; its regular part G = F − λ/(s−1) is expanded in a Taylor series at s = 2, with Cauchy's estimate on the circle |s−2| = 3/2 (where |G| ≤ 4000 (N₁N₂)²), giving ‖λ‖ ≥ (1−β)/2 · (50000 (N₁N₂)²)^(−4(1−β)) whenever Re F(β) ≤ 0 and 7/8 ≤ β < 1; Siegel's dichotomy (an exceptional zero in [1−ε/16, 1) or none, in which case χ₁ is the character mod 4) gives the ineffective constant. Characters that induce the same character as χ₁ are handled with the Euler factors (∏_{p∣n}(1−1/p) ≥ c(η)n^(−η)). Two auxiliary statements are also compared: the integral representation L(s, χ) = s∫_1^∞ A(t) t^(−s−1) dt on Re s > 0 (SiegelThm.LFunction_eq_integral, via Mathlib's Abel summation for Re s > 1, a Mellin-transform holomorphy argument and the identity theorem) and ‖∑_{k≤M} χ(k)‖ ≤ N (SiegelThm.norm_sum_Icc_le). Mathlib is the only dependency; Mathlib's continuation of ζ is not used (ζ(s) = 1/(s−1) + 1 − s∫_1^∞{t}t^(−s−1) dt is proved directly). Three statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: CH89.lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular_sqrt7
records.entry_name: Chetwynd–Hilton 1989: regular graphs of degree at least ½(√7 − 1)|V| are 1-factorizable
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of Theorem 2 of Chetwynd and Hilton, "1-factorizing regular graphs of high degree — an improved bound" (Discrete Math. 75 (1989)): a d-regular simple graph of even order with d ≥ ½(√7 − 1)|V| (≈ 0.823|V|) is d-edge-colourable (CH89.lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular_sqrt7), with the integer form |V| = 2n, 7n² ≤ (d + n)² (CH89.lineGraph_colorable_of_isRegular_nat). The article's proof of Theorem 1 contains an unjustified step ("we may moreover suppose that x_j comes before w_j in the list (r_m, …, r_t, l_1, …, l_m)"), which fails for an arbitrary maximal matching M₀; the formalization repairs it by choosing M₀ to minimize −K·#covered + max(T, T′), T = u_Y − u_X − μ, ordering the edges of M₀ (mixed ones outside, XX/YY alternately) and pairing X with Y by Hall's theorem with one dummy, so that at most one pair is bad, which the article's extra step q + 1 absorbs. The constant ½(√7 − 1) of the article is obtained exactly. Theorem 1 (staircase classes peeled off as near 1-factors, core of Theorem 5, re-insertion of v* and w) is assembled from the pinned dependency PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000016; Lemma 3 (a pair with r(r − 1) ≤ (2n − 1)p common non-neighbours) and the parameter inequality r(r − 1) − (2n − 1)(5n − 3d − 1) = (d + n)² − 7n² + n + 1 are proved here. Two statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: CoreDeg2.hiltonZhao_critical
records.entry_name: Graphs whose core has maximum degree two: Hilton–Zhao structure and the Cariolaro–Cariolaro theorem
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on finite simple graphs G whose core (the vertices of maximum degree Δ) has maximum degree at most two, stated as: every vertex of degree Δ has at most two neighbours of degree Δ. Hilton–Zhao (1992): if G is connected and not Δ-edge-colourable, then G − e is Δ-edge-colourable for every edge e, every vertex has at least two neighbours of degree Δ (so the core is 2-regular), and every vertex has degree at least Δ − 1, with equality somewhere when Δ ≥ 3 (hiltonZhao_critical, hiltonZhao_two_le, hiltonZhao_core_regular, hiltonZhao_min_degree, hiltonZhao_min_degree_eq); corollaries: class one when some vertex of degree Δ has at most one neighbour of degree Δ, or some vertex has degree at most Δ − 2. For Δ = 3: a connected class-two graph is a petal graph (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 3: degrees 2 or 3, the degree-3 vertices induce a 2-regular graph, degree-2 vertices have only degree-3 neighbours) and 3|E| = 4|V|; and if some component of the core carries no internal petal (no vertex of degree below 3 adjacent to two of its vertices) then G is 3-edge-colourable (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 7, for a single core cycle). The graph P* (Petersen minus a vertex) is defined on Fin 9, proved isomorphic to the Petersen graph minus a vertex, and shown to satisfy the hypotheses, to be connected, of class two and not overfull. Cariolaro–Cariolaro (2003): a connected graph with Δ = 3 whose core has maximum degree at most two is not 3-edge-colourable if and only if it is isomorphic to P* (cariolaro_iff, cariolaro). The proof recolours one core cycle with its petals in a colouring of G − e (criticality): a combinatorial chorded-cycle lemma (a cyclic sequence of vertices with chords and external restrictions has a proper 3-edge-colouring whose missing colours differ along chords and avoid the restrictions, unless it is the hexagon with three antipodal chords or a chordless odd cycle with constant restrictions) proved by induction with safe local reductions; the arc reduction rests on a finite automaton whose reachable states are checked by decide. Vizing's theorem and Vizing's adjacency lemma are lake dependencies on PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009; Kempe chains and their end-point lemma come from the former.

records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization of results on finite simple graphs G whose core (the vertices of maximum degree Δ) has maximum degree at most two, stated as: every vertex of degree Δ has at most two neighbours of degree Δ. Hilton–Zhao (1992): if G is connected and not Δ-edge-colourable, then G − e is Δ-edge-colourable for every edge e, every vertex has at least two neighbours of degree Δ (so the core is 2-regular), and every vertex has degree at least Δ − 1, with equality somewhere when Δ ≥ 3 (hiltonZhao_critical, hiltonZhao_two_le, hiltonZhao_core_regular, hiltonZhao_min_degree, hiltonZhao_min_degree_eq); corollaries: class one when some vertex of degree Δ has at most one neighbour of degree Δ, or some vertex has degree at most Δ − 2. For Δ = 3: a connected class-two graph is a petal graph (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 3: degrees 2 or 3, the degree-3 vertices induce a 2-regular graph, degree-2 vertices have only degree-3 neighbours) and 3|E| = 4|V|; and if some component of the core carries no internal petal (no vertex of degree below 3 adjacent to two of its vertices) then G is 3-edge-colourable (Cariolaro–Cariolaro Lemma 7, for a single core cycle). The graph P* (Petersen minus a vertex) is defined on Fin 9, proved isomorphic to the Petersen graph minus a vertex, and shown to satisfy the hypotheses, to be connected, of class two and not overfull. Cariolaro–Cariolaro (2003): a connected graph with Δ = 3 whose core has maximum degree at most two is not 3-edge-colourable if and only if it is isomorphic to P* (cariolaro_iff, cariolaro). The proof recolours one core cycle with its petals in a colouring of G − e (criticality): a combinatorial chorded-cycle lemma (a cyclic sequence of vertices with chords and external restrictions has a proper 3-edge-colouring whose missing colours differ along chords and avoid the restrictions, unless it is the hexagon with three antipodal chords or a chordless odd cycle with constant restrictions) proved by induction with safe local reductions; the arc reduction rests on a finite automaton whose reachable states are checked by decide. Vizing's theorem and Vizing's adjacency lemma are lake dependencies on PALOMAR-2026-10-15-000004 and PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009; Kempe chains and their end-point lemma come from the former.

records.name: ErdosWilson.colorable_of_subsingleton_maxDegree
records.entry_name: Erdős–Wilson: almost every graph is of class one
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the theorem of Erdős and Wilson (1977) that almost every graph is of class one: among the 2^C(n,2) labelled graphs on Fin n, the proportion whose line graph is Δ(G)-colourable tends to 1 (erdos_wilson). On the way it proves that almost every graph has a unique vertex of maximum degree (tendsto_unique_maxDegree) and that a graph with at most one vertex of maximum degree is of class one (colorable_of_subsingleton_maxDegree, the special case of Fournier's theorem imported from PALOMAR-2026-11-08-000009). The probabilistic part is a second-moment argument with explicit binomial estimates: with X the number of vertices of degree at least a threshold k, P(X = 0) ≤ 1/(n tl_k) + bp_{k-1}^2/(4 tl_k^2) and P(two distinct vertices of equal degree ≥ k) ≤ n^2 Σ_{i ≥ k-1} bp_i^2, where bp, tl are the point probabilities and upper tails of Bin(n-2, 1/2); the joint law of two degrees is computed exactly by a symmetric-difference (translation) argument on the set of graphs, and k is chosen adaptively. Only qualitative statements (limits) are stated; no rate of convergence is claimed. Three statements; no definitions beyond Mathlib's.

records.name: GwPower.theorem4
records.entry_name: Gallai–van der Waerden numbers from m-th power residue colourings
records.doc: A Lean 4 and Mathlib proof of two lower-bound constructions for the Gallai–van der Waerden numbers GW(r; k, l) of Mao, Ozeki, Robertson and Wang (the least M such that for every n ≥ M, every exact r-colouring of {1, …, n} contains a rainbow k-term or a monochromatic l-term arithmetic progression), for rainbow (m + 1)-term progressions and every m. Let p > l ≥ 2 be a prime with p ≡ 1 (mod m) such that (i) for every i in {0, …, m} the m residues j − i (j ≠ i, 0 ≤ j ≤ m) do not lie in m distinct m-th power classes modulo p, and (ii) no l consecutive integers in [1, p − 1] lie in one class. Theorem 4: colouring x in [1, (l − 1)p] by (x − 1)^((p − 1)/m) mod p (the m-th power class of x − 1, and a new colour 0 on the zero class x ≡ 1 (mod p)) uses exactly m + 1 colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term and no monochromatic l-term progression, so GW(m + 1; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p. Theorem 8: if instead the zero class 1 + kp (0 ≤ k ≤ l − 1) of [1, (l − 1)p + 1] is coloured by s ≥ 2 new colours z(k), where z uses all s colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term progression, the colouring uses exactly m + s colours and is good, so GW(m + s; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p + 1. The formalization proves both theorems for every such m, l, p (and s, z), the resulting bounds for GW (unconditionally for every threshold with the defining property, and for the number itself given that a threshold exists), and five instances with l = 4: GW(4; 4, 4) > 327, GW(5; 5, 4) > 1059, GW(6; 6, 4) > 2253, GW(6; 4, 4) > 328 and GW(8; 5, 4) > 1060.

Theorem 4: colouring x in [1, (l − 1)p] by (x − 1)^((p − 1)/m) mod p (the m-th power class of x − 1, and a new colour 0 on the zero class x ≡ 1 (mod p)) uses exactly m + 1 colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term and no monochromatic l-term progression, so GW(m + 1; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p. Theorem 8: if instead the zero class 1 + kp (0 ≤ k ≤ l − 1) of [1, (l − 1)p + 1] is coloured by s ≥ 2 new colours z(k), where z uses all s colours and has no rainbow (m + 1)-term progression, the colouring uses exactly m + s colours and is good, so GW(m + s; m + 1, l) > (l − 1)p + 1. The formalization proves both theorems for every such m, l, p (and s, z), the resulting bounds for GW (unconditionally for every threshold with the defining property, and for the number itself given that a threshold exists), and five instances with l = 4: GW(4; 4, 4) > 327, GW(5; 5, 4) > 1059, GW(6; 6, 4) > 2253, GW(6; 4, 4) > 328 and GW(8; 5, 4) > 1060.

records.name: Couret.PalomarSingleton.singleton_collision_iff
records.entry_name: Singleton-overlap four-point square collisions and C4 × C4 subgroups
records.doc: For any decidable abelian group, two four-point finite supports with one common point and identical full labelled ordered squares exist exactly when Z/4Z × Z/4Z embeds additively. The ambient group need not be cyclic or finite. No novelty assessment or independent human review is asserted.

records.name: VizingAdj.vizing_adjacency_lemma
records.entry_name: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma and Kierstead's lemma, as a standalone module
records.doc: A thin wrapper that exposes, with Mathlib definitions only, the basic recolouring lemmas of edge-colouring theory proved inside PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009 (overfull-critical-graphs). vizing_adjacency_lemma (Vizing 1965): if G is of class two (its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable) and G − xy is Δ(G)-edge-colourable, then x has at least Δ − d(y) + 1 neighbours of degree Δ other than y. critical_two_maxDegree_neighbours: every vertex of a Δ-critical graph has at least two neighbours of degree Δ. multifan_lemma (Stiebitz–Scheide–Toft–Favrholdt, Theorem 2.1): for a Δ(G)-colouring of G − x y₀ of a class-two graph, a multifan at x is elementary and x is joined to every fan vertex by a path coloured with any colour free at x and any colour free at that vertex. kierstead_lemma (Kierstead 1984): a Kierstead path whose interior vertices y₂, …, y_{L−2} have degree below Δ is elementary. Partial edge colourings are symmetric functions V → V → Option (Fin k); five definitions (proper partial edge colouring, colouring of G − ab, free colour, multifan, Kierstead path). The only new proof is the corollary (from Vizing's lemma) and the translation to the colourings of the Vizing entry.

records.name: VizingAdj.critical_two_maxDegree_neighbours
records.entry_name: Vizing's adjacency lemma, the multifan lemma and Kierstead's lemma, as a standalone module
records.doc: A thin wrapper that exposes, with Mathlib definitions only, the basic recolouring lemmas of edge-colouring theory proved inside PALOMAR-2026-11-04-000009 (overfull-critical-graphs). vizing_adjacency_lemma (Vizing 1965): if G is of class two (its line graph is not Δ(G)-colourable) and G − xy is Δ(G)-edge-colourable, then x has at least Δ − d(y) + 1 neighbours of degree Δ other than y. critical_two_maxDegree_neighbours: every vertex of a Δ-critical graph has at least two neighbours of degree Δ. multifan_lemma (Stiebitz–Scheide–Toft–Favrholdt, Theorem 2.1): for a Δ(G)-colouring of G − x y₀ of a class-two graph, a multifan at x is elementary and x is joined to every fan vertex by a path coloured with any colour free at x and any colour free at that vertex. kierstead_lemma (Kierstead 1984): a Kierstead path whose interior vertices y₂, …, y_{L−2} have degree below Δ is elementary. Partial edge colourings are symmetric functions V → V → Option (Fin k); five definitions (proper partial edge colouring, colouring of G − ab, free colour, multifan, Kierstead path). The only new proof is the corollary (from Vizing's lemma) and the translation to the colourings of the Vizing entry.

records.name: PaperP1Registry.V2.QuadraticLimits.source_probability
records.entry_name: P1 publication: Optimal quadratic approximation and Poisson scales
records.doc: The full original run-count law has optimal quadratic Poisson–Charlier error with exact mean and second factorial cumulant, a uniform mean-bias bound and eventual probability status. Exact and nominal Poisson total variation have their distinct remainder powers and the same moving residue equivalent. Every fixed polynomial weight and factorial moment, the zero-count probability, and the literal integer quantization and cost of replacing the exact mean are recorded.

records.name: PerkovicReed.one_factorization_of_ge
records.entry_name: Asymptotic 1-factorization of dense regular graphs (Perković–Reed, via Vaughan)
records.doc: A Lean 4 / Mathlib proof of the asymptotic form of the Chetwynd–Hilton 1-factorization conjecture (Perković and Reed 1997, Häggkvist): for every ε > 0 there is N such that every d-regular simple graph on 2n vertices with n ≥ N and d ≥ (1 + ε) n is 1-factorizable, i.e. its line graph is d-colourable (one_factorization); the integer form with (q + 1) n ≤ q d for q ≥ 1 is one_factorization_of_ge. The proof follows Vaughan (arXiv:1010.5192) for multiplicity 1: a balanced bipartition A, Aᶜ with |d_A(v) − d_{Aᶜ}(v)| < s for every vertex (Lemma 13, here by a counting Chernoff bound with no probability theory), equitable colourings of the two sides with matched class sizes (Vizing and McDiarmid's equalisation, from the registered Vizing entry), 5-edge alternating-path exchanges until every colour class is a perfect matching, completion of the classes of the leftover inside edges by Hall's theorem, and a decomposition of the remaining regular bipartite graph into perfect matchings (Hall). Vaughan's sizes n^{2/3} and n^{5/6} are replaced by linear sizes s = ⌊a/(200q)⌋ and t = ⌊a/6⌋ with a = ⌊n/q⌋; N is explicit, N = L (512 L³ + 4) with L = 200 q² for d ≥ (1 + 1/q) n (very large). No definitions beyond Mathlib's. Two statements.

records.name: Smale.P030.Rows.thm_1_1
records.entry_name: Smale's mean value constant equals 4
records.doc:
A Lean 4 proof that Smale's mean value constant equals 4. For a complex polynomial p of degree d >= 2 with p(0) = 0 and p'(0) != 0, let S(p) be the minimum of |p(c)/(c p'(0))| over the critical points c of p, let K(d) be the supremum of S(p) over all such p of degree d, and let K* be the supremum of K(d) over d >= 2. In 1981 Smale proved K* <= 4 and asked whether 4 can be replaced by 1 (and asked it again in 2000). The formalization proves K* = lim_{d -> oo} K(d) = 4, which is Theorem 1.1 of D. Goel, "Smale's mean value constant (1981) equals 4". It also proves Smale's bound K(d) <= 4, that K(d) does not decrease with d, and that K(d) < 4 for every d.
Comparison with Smale's conjecture. Smale asked whether K* = 1. That was disproved in 2026 (Adamczewski's Lean disproof; Adamczewski and Colbrook). Jatar and Ng then proved K* > 1.1018, and the author proved K* > 1.1559. This project does not prove the conjecture: it answers Smale's question in the negative. K* equals 4, Smale's own bound, so no constant smaller than 4 works for all degrees. In each single degree the constant stays below 4: K(d) <= 4^((d-2)/(d-1)) (Beardon, Minda and Ng, 2002), and K(d) < 4 - 2.263/sqrt(d) for d >= 8 (Crane, 2007). So the supremum K* is not attained.

records.name: PlantholtShan.hakimi
records.entry_name: Plantholt–Shan: the overfull conjecture for graphs of minimum degree at least (1 + ε) n
records.doc: M. J. Plantholt and S. Shan, Edge coloring graphs with large minimum degree (arXiv:2105.05286), in Lean 4 / Mathlib. theorem_1_2 (Theorem 1.2): for every ε > 0 there is N such that a graph G on 2n vertices, n ≥ N, with δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n is Δ(G)-edge-colourable iff it has no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (PlantholtShan.HasOverfullSubgraph, the definition of the registered plantholt-overfull-criterion entry restated in the challenge: an odd set of at least three vertices spanning more than Δ(G)(|S| − 1)/2 edges). theorem_1_3b (Theorem 1.3, Condition (b)): two vertices x ≠ y with d(x) = d(y) ≥ (1/2 + 3ε/2) n, all other vertices of degree Δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n and Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ (1/2 − ε/2) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N. theorem_1_3c (Condition (c)): Δ(G) − δ(G) ≥ n^{6/7}, at least n^{6/7} vertices of degree δ(G), at least n + 1 of degree Δ(G) and δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N (n^{6/7} as a real power). Condition (a) (regular graphs) is the registered asymptotic-one-factorization entry. lemma_2_11 (Lemma 2.11): a bipartite graph with sides of size n, all degrees at least t and at most t vertices of degree below n/2 has a perfect matching. Kept from version 1: hakimi (Theorem 2.5), hamiltonConnected_of_minDegree (Theorem 2.6, δ ≥ n/2 + 1) and exists_spanning_paths (Lemma 2.12). The thresholds N are explicit but huge (e.g. (2^60 q + 1)^21 with 1/q < ε) and not optimized. Two definitions (IsMultigraph, HasOverfullSubgraph). Seven statements.

records.name: PlantholtShan.theorem_1_2
records.entry_name: Plantholt–Shan: the overfull conjecture for graphs of minimum degree at least (1 + ε) n
records.doc: M. J. Plantholt and S. Shan, Edge coloring graphs with large minimum degree (arXiv:2105.05286), in Lean 4 / Mathlib. theorem_1_2 (Theorem 1.2): for every ε > 0 there is N such that a graph G on 2n vertices, n ≥ N, with δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n is Δ(G)-edge-colourable iff it has no Δ(G)-overfull subgraph (PlantholtShan.HasOverfullSubgraph, the definition of the registered plantholt-overfull-criterion entry restated in the challenge: an odd set of at least three vertices spanning more than Δ(G)(|S| − 1)/2 edges). theorem_1_3b (Theorem 1.3, Condition (b)): two vertices x ≠ y with d(x) = d(y) ≥ (1/2 + 3ε/2) n, all other vertices of degree Δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n and Δ(G) − δ(G) ≤ (1/2 − ε/2) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N. theorem_1_3c (Condition (c)): Δ(G) − δ(G) ≥ n^{6/7}, at least n^{6/7} vertices of degree δ(G), at least n + 1 of degree Δ(G) and δ(G) ≥ (1 + ε) n give χ′ = Δ for n ≥ N (n^{6/7} as a real power). records.name: PaperP1Registry.V2.CumulantsOptimality.factorial_source
records.entry_name: P1 publication: Factorial cumulants and optimal quadratic error
records.doc: Actual heterogeneous factorial-count identities, with repeated-index corrections, and the unconditional optimal 41/30 power for the third factorial cumulant. Absolute triple activity has the same upper exponent. The fourth-cumulant decomposition retains the positive compatible quartic mass and distinguishes 5/3 and 3/2 errors; the exact quadratic Poisson–Charlier approximation has matching 4/3 upper and lower power bounds.

records.name: PaperP1Registry.V2.PairsChannels.complete_pair_profile
records.entry_name: P1 publication: Arithmetic pair profiles and finite channel heights
records.doc: Positive and signed arithmetic profiles over ordered separated pairs of multiplicative runs, including both moving residue phases and the explicit two-channel probability law. Every fixed finite channel-height truncation has a literal next-height cumulant and law remainder and a sharp total-variation equivalent. Weighted nonaligned pairs, the closed height-five correction, and the height-six phase are included with their exact coefficients.

records.name: OeisA2454.conjecture
records.entry_name: OEIS A002454: the odd-order permanent identity (She–Sun–Xia)
records.doc: For every n and every primitive complex (2n+1)-th root of unity ζ, the permanent of the 2n × 2n matrix with entries 1 on the diagonal and (1 + ζ^(j−k))/(1 − ζ^(j−k)) off it equals 4^n (n!)^2/(2n+1). Zhi-Wei Sun posed the identity in OEIS A002454 (2022), and She, Sun and Xia proved it (arXiv:2208.12167, Theorem 1.3(ii)). The proof formalizes the determinant approach of Guo, Li, Tao and Wei.

records.name: DsrgRank.ClosedNbhd_no_50_11_7_0_3
records.entry_name: Nonexistence of directed strongly regular graphs by rank arguments
records.doc: Lean 4 and Mathlib proofs that no directed strongly regular graph exists for 28 parameter sets (v, k, t, λ, μ). A directed strongly regular graph is a 0-1 matrix A with zero diagonal, all row and column sums equal to k and A² = tI + λA + μ(J − I − A). Nine of the parameter sets are those of the paper below: (50, 11, 7, 0, 3), (68, 13, 7, 0, 3), (100, 16, 7, 0, 3), (108, 19, 9, 0, 4), (55, 16, 12, 1, 6), (66, 10, 5, 4, 1), (91, 12, 6, 5, 1), (96, 15, 10, 9, 1) and (28, 6, 3, 2, 1); the tenth set of the paper, (48, 9, 5, 0, 2), is not formalized. The same lemmas exclude eight further sets, and a formalized complement lemma excludes eleven complementary sets. The proofs compare the rank of A − θI, for a root θ of the quadratic x² − (λ − μ)x − (t − μ), with a submatrix of A prescribed at one vertex. For (28, 6, 3, 2, 1) one case is a SAT refutation whose LRAT certificate the Lean kernel checks with decide +kernel. The theorems use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
